rubric_items.reason: All six acceptance criteria map to REQ-1..REQ-17. The edge cases (both Inactive, empty reason, cancellation reason) are covered by REQ-11, REQ-18 and REQ-19. How the reason is passed is in Out of scope with a reason.
Each REQ covers one behaviour with a condition a tester can check. Doctor and patient, and the Cancelled and No-show states, are split into separate REQs.
Every REQ marked known cites ticket lines, the baseline or IDE answers A-01..A-03. Nothing is invented, and REQ-18 was confirmed by the user before it was marked known.
The ticket and baseline do not clash. The ticket's closed-appointment and booking rules match intent-baseline booking-rules and closed-appointments, and REQ-12 and REQ-14 cite both.
The questions were few, offered real options and had proposed defaults. Part of Q-02 was already answered by the data model, which has separate reason and cancellation_reason columns.
Plain wording, and the glossary terms Cancelled, No-show, Scheduled, Completed and Inactive are used consistently. The missing glossary entry for 'Reason for visit' is stated openly.

findings.text: Q-02 asked whether 'reason for visit' means the appointment's own field and not the cancellation reason. The context pack already answers this: the appointment table has separate reason and cancellation_reason columns.

cites.quote: Is it the appointment's own reason-for-visit field (not the cancellation reason a Cancelled appointment also has)?

findings.suggested_fix: Cite the db-schema columns as the basis for REQ-6 and REQ-19, and keep only the remaining product question if one is still needed.

findings.text: Out of scope says the ticket requires the appointment API to stay unchanged. The ticket only says booking rules stay unchanged and never mentions the appointment API.

cites.quote: Any change to booking rules APT-1 to APT-4 or to the appointment API: the ticket requires them unchanged.
Booking from there follows the existing rules unchanged

findings.suggested_fix: Remove 'or to the appointment API', or give it a separate reason (for example, a design-step decision) instead of crediting it to the ticket.
